learningObjective: Choose between account keys, the three kinds of SAS, and Entra ID. Create and cancel SAS safely with stored access policies. Rotate or turn off keys without breaking apps.
engineer: Account keys: every account has two, key1 and key2. They give full access to everything in the account.
Regenerating a key: the old key stops working at once, and so does every account SAS and service SAS signed with it.

Rotating keys without an outage: move apps to key2; regenerate key1; move apps back to key1; regenerate key2. Keep keys in Key Vault, set a key expiration policy, and watch for old keys with Azure Policy or Advisor.

Turning off Shared Key (allowSharedKeyAccess = false): blocks the account keys and every SAS signed with a key. Entra ID sign-in and user delegation SAS keep working. Check first that the portal, AzCopy and your apps use Entra ID.

The three SAS types: account SAS, for one or more services, signed with an account key; service SAS, for one service, signed with an account key, and the only kind that can use a stored access policy; user delegation SAS, for blobs and Data Lake only, signed with a key you get by signing in with Entra ID.
User delegation SAS rules: it lasts at most 7 days. Creating one needs the generateUserDelegationKey permission, for example from the Storage Blob Delegator role.

Reading a SAS URL: sv, the version; ss and srt, which services and resource types (account SAS); sp, the permissions (r read, w write, l list…); st and se, start and expiry time; sip, allowed IP addresses; spr, HTTPS only; si, the stored access policy; sig, the signature. If any of these don't match the request, you get 403.
Stored access policies: up to five per container, file share, queue or table. A service SAS can point to one and take its permissions and expiry from it.

Cancelling a SAS: if it uses a stored access policy, delete or rename the policy (it takes up to 30 seconds). If it doesn't, you must regenerate the key that signed it. For a user delegation SAS, revoke the user delegation keys.
Good habits: short expiry; only the permissions needed; HTTPS only; limit IPs with sip; set a SAS expiration policy on the account; use Entra ID instead of keys whenever the app supports it.

example.title: Partner downloads you can cancel
body: A partner needs to read and list the reports container for one month. The admin creates a stored access policy called 'partner-read' (read and list, 30 days). Then they give the partner a service SAS that uses this policy.

The contract ends early. The admin deletes the policy, and the partner's SAS stops working within seconds. No keys are rotated, so no other app breaks. Internal apps already use managed identities with Storage Blob Data Reader, so later Shared Key is turned off.

architectureDecisions: Use Entra ID first: apps sign in with managed identities. For links you hand out, use a user delegation SAS.
If you must use a service SAS, attach a stored access policy: then you can cancel it without rotating keys.
Rotate keys automatically: with Key Vault, switching between key1 and key2.

misconceptions.myth: You can delete a SAS to cancel it.
misconceptions.reality: No. A SAS is just a URL. Cancel it by deleting its stored access policy, or by regenerating the key that signed it.

misconceptions.myth: An account SAS can use a stored access policy.
misconceptions.reality: No. Only a service SAS can.

misconceptions.myth: Turning off Shared Key breaks every SAS.
misconceptions.reality: No. User delegation SAS keeps working, because it's signed with Entra ID.

comparisons.difference: Like a SAS, but signed with IAM credentials (closer to a user delegation SAS). There is nothing like a stored access policy.
No secrets that can leak. Access is per identity and logged. Better than keys and SAS.

troubleshooting.symptom: 403 'Signature did not match' for a SAS that used to work.
troubleshooting.cause: The key that signed it was regenerated, or the URL was changed.
troubleshooting.fix: Create a new SAS with the current key, or use a stored access policy or a user delegation SAS.

troubleshooting.symptom: 403 'This request is not authorized to perform this operation using this permission'.
troubleshooting.cause: sp doesn't include that action (for example l for list).
troubleshooting.fix: Create a SAS with the permission letter you need.

troubleshooting.symptom: The SAS works on office Wi-Fi but not on mobile data.
troubleshooting.cause: sip limits the SAS to certain IP addresses.
troubleshooting.fix: Widen or remove the IP limit.

troubleshooting.symptom: The portal's 'Switch to access key' fails after turning off Shared Key.
troubleshooting.cause: Key access isn't allowed any more.
troubleshooting.fix: Use Entra ID sign-in with a data role.

configuration.limits: Five stored access policies per container, share, queue or table
User delegation SAS: 7 days at most
Policy changes take up to 30 seconds
configuration.permissions: Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/listkeys/action to read keys (Storage Account Key Operator Service Role, or Contributor)
Storage Blob Delegator (or a data role) for user delegation SAS
configuration.prerequisites: For user delegation SAS: an Entra identity with generateUserDelegationKey and a data role
